artworks.title: The Abduction of Ganymede
artworks.description: Dresden's Rembrandt subverts the beautiful-youth tradition: a terrified, bawling infant snatched in the eagle's grip, urinating in fright — the cupbearer's rape made earthbound and unheroic.

artworks.title: The Rape of Ganymede
artworks.description: Prado canvas for Philip IV's Torre de la Parada: Jupiter's eagle sweeps the Trojan youth into the heavens where he will serve as cupbearer of the gods — Ovid's Metamorphoses in Baroque flight.

artworks.title: The Abduction of Ganymede
artworks.description: Vienna companion to Jupiter and Io: the eagle lifts Ganymede from a wooded hillside as the boy turns toward the viewer, his dog barking from the ground below.

popCulture.title: Ganymede (moon)
popCulture.description: Jupiter's largest moon — and the largest in the solar system — took the cupbearer's name, so the Trojan youth still orbits the king of the gods.
